rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The presentation before God is a metaphor for accounting, likened to a ruler reviewing his army.
rows.anchor: Burada “arz” hesabdan mecaz olup bir hükümdara askerinin ahvâlini görmesi için arzolunmalarına teşbih tarîkiyle ifade olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is not merely an outward presentation like worldly reviews: no hidden matter remains concealed, as 14:48 also describes.
rows.anchor: Öyle arzolunursunuz ki gizli bir hâliniz kalmaz وَبَرَزُوا۟ لِلَّهِ ٱلْوَٰحِدِ ٱلْقَهَّارِ

rows.speaker: Ebû Mûsâ el-Eş‘arî
rows.claim: The Prophet says people are presented three times on Judgment Day: the first two involve disputation and excuses; at the third, pages fly into their hands.
rows.anchor: Ebû Mûsâ el-Eş‘arî radıyallahu anh’tan rivayet [5327] etmişlerdir ki Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem şöyle buyurdu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book is the register of lifetime deeds recorded by angels, or its balanced summary or documentary proof that the account was reviewed; 17:13 describes it.
rows.anchor: Bu kitab Sûre-i İsrâ’da وَكُلَّ إِنسَٰنٍ أَلْزَمْنَٰهُ طَٰٓئِرَهُۥ فِى عُنُقِهِۦ وَنُخْرِجُ لَهُۥ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ كِتَٰبًۭا يَلْقَىٰهُ مَنشُورًا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book's daily original is already attached to each person's neck in the memory that preserves the day's record.
rows.anchor: Ve bunun esas yevmiyesi insanın her gün kendi hâfızasında kendi boynuna asılıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yamīn, opposite shimāl, means the right hand or side and connotes strength, honesty, propriety, purity, good fortune, good, and gain.
rows.anchor: Burada “yemîn”, “şimal” mukabili olduğundan sağ el, sağ taraf demektir ki sağlamlık, dürüstlük, uygunluk, temizlik, uğur, hayr ve kesb ifade eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Right-hand action symbolizes acting properly for oneself; the left signals the reverse, while putting something behind means neglect or leaving it to others. The imagery also places good-deed angels to the right, bad-deed angels to the left, and associates the angel/right and Satan/left.
rows.anchor: Sağ eliyle yapması sağlam, dürüst, uygun, kendi lehinde iyi yapması; sol eliyle yapması da tersine yapması; arkaya atması ise ihmal etmesi, başkasından umması mânalarını ifade eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying the book is given, rather than self-written, reflects that God's enabling, decree, judgment, and execution govern the outcome.
rows.anchor: “Verilmesi” tâbiri dahi hepsi Allah’ın tevfîki, takdîri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although creation and command belong to God, responsibility is tied to voluntary deeds: by choosing them, a person effectively dictates the record to the angels like a scribe.
rows.anchor: insanın mes’ûliyeti ihtiyârî fiillerine rabtedilmiş olduğu cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When deeds are upright and accurately weighed, the book is a sound, valid record in one's favor; the favorable verdict is delivered into the right hand and the account made easy.
rows.anchor: o defterler kendi lehinde olmak üzere sağlam, muteber, kendi hesâbına güzel yazı ile yazılmış bir defter olacağından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should read their daily record and take stock before God, preparing for tomorrow in accordance with 17:14 and 59:18.
rows.anchor: her gün kendi boynuna geçirilmiş kitabı, yevmiye defteri demek olan hâfızasında kendi nefsini ve meleklere yazdırdığı amellerini hak gözüyle okuyup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone who never audits himself has put the matter behind him, dictating a record heedlessly and without considering the harm.
rows.anchor: Vicdânında her gün Hakk’a karşı nefsini muhasebe etmeyen kimse işini arkaya atmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who distort right and wrong fill the record with bad deeds and liabilities; angels record facts faithfully, so the wrongdoer has signed his own destiny against himself.
rows.anchor: meleklerin tuttuğu zabıt onun aleyhinde olarak muameleyi olduğu gibi göstermiş ve ona imza ettirilmiş olmak haysiyetiyle sağlam, doğru ve haddizâtında muteber bulunduğundan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer's account is reviewed by a friend and its verdict handed over favorably; the disbeliever's is reviewed by a hated opponent and given against him in the left hand.
rows.anchor: huzûr-i Hak’ta yüzü ak olarak hesâbı dost tarafından görülmüş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hāʾummu is rendered as an invitation to take or come receive the book.
rows.anchor: Ha işte size alın, gelin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invites others to read the record as an expression of hope in the account's outcome, joy before fellow believers, or proof of entry to Paradise.
rows.anchor: hesâbına ümidini veya neticesinde ihvânına ferah ve neşâtını veya cennete giderken pasaportunu göstermek üzere der ki

rows.speaker: Ekser müfessirîn
rows.claim: Most commentators take zann to mean prior knowledge and conviction: he believed with certainty that he would meet his account and therefore kept it carefully.
rows.anchor: Ekser müfessirîn burada zannı önceden ilim ve itikad

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: An alternative is that, despite believing in the account, he feared his many shortcomings and meager good deeds would leave him with liabilities exceeding his credits.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh bazılarının dediği gibi bu, şu demek de olabilir: Ben hesâba inanmakla beraber birçok kusurlar ettiğimi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers that alternative: even tiny deeds he never noticed were valued and rewarded through the Merciful Lord's pure grace, not his own merit; this is more apparent and ethically instructive.
rows.anchor: Bu mâna hem daha zâhir hem daha ahlâkīdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling life itself pleased is a rhetorical attribution for emphasis: the person is pleased and beloved, while life, beautified by his character and works, is also pleased with him.
rows.anchor: mübalağa için yaşayışın kendisine nisbet edilmiştir ki yalnız o kendisi râzı ve hoşnut olmakla kalmayacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The high afterlife Paradise is pure happiness and blessing, unlike the lower world, which mixes pleasures with hardship and pain.
rows.anchor: dünya cenneti gibi süfliyyât ile, mihnet ve âlâm ile karışık değil, hâlis bir saâdet ü nimet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paradise's fruits and blessings hang nearby, ready to be picked; the inhabitants may eat and drink in comfort for what they sent ahead.
rows.anchor: devşirimleri, yani iktitaf olunacak yemişleri, meyveleri, nimetleri, uzakta değil, yakında sarkıp duruyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islāf means making an advance delivery or offering against something deferred.
rows.anchor: veresiye olarak önceden arz u takdim etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In legal usage, salaf or salam is a transaction in which payment is made upfront and the goods are deferred.
rows.anchor: Onun için şer‘an da “selef”, ta‘bîr-i âharla “selem” denilen muameleye ıtlak olunur ki para peşin mal veresiye olmak üzere yapılan bir alışveriş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aslaftum also evokes giving God a good loan (57:18) and the benefit of presenting something to and serving a superior.
rows.anchor: hem وَأَقْرَضُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ قَرْضًا حَسَنًۭا [el-Hadîd 57/18] mânasına hem de büyüğe takdim etmek ve ona hizmet eylemekteki büyük istifadeye işaret buyurulmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These acts must be advanced in ease before death, illness, or trial; the best opportunity is youth, since distress leaves no room to give or serve.
rows.anchor: Geçmiş günlerde, yahut bugünkü derdin bulunmadığı, hâlin müsâid, başların sağ ve sâlim olduğu boş ve müsâid günlerde

rows.speaker: Allah
rows.claim: A report portrays God telling His friends that He watched them endure thirst and hunger for His path in worldly life, and now invites them to eat and drink in return.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunmuştur ki o gün Allah teâlâ şöyle buyurur: “Ey dostlarım! Dünyada size Ben çok vakit bakardım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who waste their available days on endless desire or lose their capital to the unworthy face regret and deprivation.
rows.anchor: vay o günleri boşuna geçirenlere veya

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some do ostensibly good works for people, ostentation, or others' pleasure rather than God; rewards from people disappear like a bankrupt's assets, leaving only pain and deprivation before God.
rows.anchor: hayır denebilecek şeyler yaparlar amma Hak için Allah için değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their deeds end in loss, so these are people who wrote their books backward and left-handed.
rows.anchor: Bütün o Hâkka onların başında patlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun hā refers to the first death, although death is not stated explicitly; the surah's opening and the speaker's awakening at the account imply it.
rows.anchor: ah nolaydı o bu هَا zamiri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāḍiya means decisively finishing something, cutting it off, and issuing and executing a final judgment.
rows.anchor: bir işi tamamıyla kesip atmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wishes death had ended everything and rescued him; now, amid a calamity worse than death, he longs for death again as an escape, not merely as a past possibility.
rows.anchor: ölümden kaçan o adamın gördüğü bu felâket içinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He now neither dies nor lives, but remains in regret and longing.
rows.anchor: ne ölür ne dirilir, sade şöyle hasret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā can be a negation or rhetorical question: what use was my wealth? It helped him not at all; if it helped anyone, it was others, while he kept regret and punishment.
rows.anchor: neye yaradı benden yana malım? Hiçbir şeye yaramadı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sultān may mean the sovereignty, property, government, and wealth he boasted in and relied on, or all the proofs and arguments he clung to; he is left helpless.
rows.anchor: onunla iftihar ettiğim, herkese tasallut ettiğim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This regret fits rulers and wealthy holders of power who trusted worldly dominion, punished others, but denied punishment in their own case and committed injustice.
rows.anchor: Böyle bir sözle nedâmet ve tahassür belli ki dünya saltanatına güvenip

rows.speaker: Müfessirler
rows.claim: Commentators report that Adud al-Dawla (Fannā Khusraw b. Buwayh) wrote verses celebrating wine, singers, and a drinking gathering.
rows.anchor: Müfessirler burada şu fıkrayı kaydederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem's closing line styles its author as Adud al-Dawla, king of kings, and vanquisher of fate.
rows.anchor: عــضــد الدولة وابــن ركنـهـا مــلك الأمــلاك غــلاب القــدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Soon after boasting of conquering fate, Fannā Khusraw went mad and died repeating that his wealth and authority had failed him.
rows.anchor: مَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنِّى مَالِيَهْ هَلَكَ عَنِّى سُلْطَٰنِيَهْ diye diye can verip gitmişti.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author leaves whether death ended the matter to God; the ruler who styled himself fate's conqueror was himself crushed by fate.
rows.anchor: Şimdi görülmüş bir şey varsa bu sözü defterine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final hā in kitābiyeh, hisābiyeh, māliyeh, and sultāniyeh is hāʾ al-sakt, used at pause after fatḥa and always read with sukūn; the underlying forms end in -iya.
rows.anchor: “Kitâbiyeh, hisâbiyeh, mâliyeh, sultâniyeh” fâsılalarında ها fetha üzerine vakf için hâ-i sekittir. Dâima sâkin okunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to seize him refers to the man who had just spoken about his useless wealth and power.
rows.anchor: Tutun onu yani öyle deyip duran kimseyi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are God's commands to the keepers of Hell, phrased as an implied utterance as though addressed to the useless wealth and power mentioned by the condemned man.
rows.anchor: Bu emirler taraf-ı ilâhîden zebânilere emirdir. O kimsenin ağzından o işe yaramayan mal ve sultana söyleniyormuş gibi hikâye suretinde mukadder kavl ile ifade olunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order is to bind him immediately.
rows.anchor: Hemen bağlayın onu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jahīm is a violently surging great fire, the most severe layer of Hell.
rows.anchor: cehennemin en şiddetli tabakası

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting Jahīm first restricts the destination: he is consigned to Jahīm alone, nowhere else.
rows.anchor: Burada “cahîm”in takdîmi kasr içindir, yani başka yere değil, ancak cahîme

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chain is seventy cubits long; the author says speculation about which kind of cubit it is serves no purpose.
rows.anchor: burada bu zirâ‘ın nasıl bir zirâ‘olduğu hakkında sözler söylemişlerse de lüzumsuzdur.

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Some take seventy as an idiom for abundance rather than an exact count, as in 9:80.
rows.anchor: Bazıları “yetmiş” adedi tahsis için değil, إِن تَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةًۭ [et-Tevbe 9/80] gibi çokluktan kinaye olduğunu söylemişler

rows.speaker: bazıları
rows.claim: Others retain the apparent numerical sense and leave its wisdom to God.
rows.anchor: bazıları da “zâhir olan adeddir, hikmetini Allah bilir” demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author proposes that the chain represents worldly lifetime: days or months are links, years are units, and its length is measured in cubits, so seventy cubits means seventy years.
rows.anchor: Bize öyle geliyor ki bu zincirden murad Allahu a‘lem dünyadaki ömürdür; cehenneme yuvarlanan onunla sallanır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites the saying that most lifespans in the community fall between sixty and seventy years to support seventy as a typical maximum lifespan.
rows.anchor: أَكْثـَرُ أَعْمَارِ أُ َّمتِي مَا بـَيْنَ سِت ِّينَ وَسَبْعِينَ buyurulmuş olmasına nazaran

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seventy also warns that those who reach that age without understanding the world or afterlife, repenting, or turning to faith and righteousness are unlikely to reform thereafter.
rows.anchor: yetmiş yaşına kadar dünyayı, âhireti anlamamış, tevbekâr olup iman ve salâha yüz tutmamış olanların ondan sonra salâhları müsteb‘ad bulunduğuna işaret olsa gerektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first stated reason for the punishment is that the man did not believe in God, the Great.
rows.anchor: Çünkü o kimse Allah Azîmü’ş-şân’a iman etmiyordu.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He neither looked after the poor and their food and welfare, sought remedies, or gave aid, nor encouraged others to do so; intent on ruling, he oppressed people and neglected their protection.
rows.anchor: miskin taâmına teşvik etmiyordu. Fukarâ-yı halkı gözetmiyor, onların ne yediğine bakmıyor, hâllerinden anlamıyor, bakımları çarelerini araştırmıyor, i‘ânede bulunmuyor
